description: Starts a screenshot set: 1 to 6 screenshots in store order, each with a screen name and a headline. Returns a project_handle and one upload command (bash and PowerShell forms) that sends every screenshot straight to storage; run it once, then call finish_project with the handle. Upload and call finish_project within 3 hours (an unfinished project lapses then); a finished one waits 72 hours to be opened. Nothing is public and no account is needed; the user saves the set to their account when they open the link finish_project returns.

background_color.description: #RRGGBB. Use the app's brand or accent colour if you can find it in the code. Leave it out for a neutral light background.

canvas_size.description: A canvas size from list_devices, as WIDTHxHEIGHT. Leave it out for the store default (1320x2868 for iPhone, 2048x2732 for iPad, 1080x1920 for Play).

device.description: A device id from list_devices. Defaults to iphone-17-pro-max for the App Store and pixel-11-pro for Google Play.

frame_color.description: A colour id of that device from list_devices. Leave it out to pick one that stands out from the background.

project_name.description: The app's name. It becomes the project name in the user's appdesigns library.

screens.description: One entry per screenshot, in the order the store should show them. The first sells the app.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the PNG or JPEG screenshot (no ~ or $VARIABLES; they are not expanded). Not read by the server; it goes into the upload command.

headline.description: The big line: the benefit this screen shows, 2 to 6 words, 32 characters or fewer (40 at most; longer is set smaller). Sentence case, no trailing period. Example: "See where every dollar goes".

screen_name.description: The screen or feature name, shown as the small line: 1 to 3 words, at most 24 characters. Example: "Weekly stats".

store.description: Which store the set is for.

name: create_project
title: Create a screenshot project
